column2: At a quoted price buyers want 9,000 units and sellers offer 6,000. What is the immediate imbalance?
column7: Desired purchases exceed the quantity offered by 9,000 minus 6,000. The quoted price does not clear this market.

column2: A household deposits savings at a bank, which lends to a manufacturer. Who ultimately receives financing?
column7: Funds flow from the household with surplus money through the intermediary to the firm needing finance. The household's immediate claim is on the bank.

column2: A firm buys control of a factory operator abroad. How is the cross-border holding classified?
column7: Control of a non-resident business establishes a direct investment relationship. The fact that the investor bought shares does not make this a portfolio holding.

column2: A pension fund buys a small parcel of overseas government bonds. Which external investment category applies?
column7: The fund owns negotiable debt securities without a direct investment relationship. The government's status as issuer does not turn the fund's holding into official reserves.

column2: Domestic GDP includes a completed bicycle. Why exclude the tyres already used to make it as separate final output?
column5: Their value belongs in investment income
column6: Their cost counts only when imported
column7: GDP measures final production. Counting intermediate components separately as well as the finished item would count some output twice.

column2: National output is unchanged in volume but all output prices rise 4%. Which measure rises?
column7: Nominal GDP values output at current prices. Real GDP removes the effect of price changes.

column2: A manufacturer lists three competing suppliers' quotations in dollars to compare costs. Which function of money matters here?
column7: A common unit makes the three prices comparable. No payment or transfer through time is necessary for that comparison.

column2: A tailor buys vegetables from a farmer who needs no clothes. What does money remove?
column7: A generally accepted means of payment removes the need for each side to want the particular good or service the other produces.

column2: A bank funds five-year loans with deposits customers may withdraw today. What transformation is it performing?
column7: The loans run longer than the liabilities funding them. Pooling deposits does not make the funding and lending terms identical.

column2: Which change moves a company towards direct financing by savers?
column3: Selling new notes directly to households
column4: Drawing on a syndicated bank loan
column6: Extending a mortgage with its lender
column7: The noteholders become creditors of the company. In the other cases a banking intermediary supplies the credit.

column2: A solvent bank faces unusually heavy withdrawals. What creates the immediate difficulty?
column3: Realising illiquid assets at short notice
column6: Estimating its normal annual loan growth
column7: Assets may cover liabilities in value while being difficult to realise quickly. Distressed sales can then transform a liquidity problem into losses.

column2: Which trade sends the proceeds to the issuer in the primary market?
column4: Resale of listed stock by a founder
column6: Purchase of an existing bond from a dealer
column7: The issuer receives the subscription money when new securities are sold. Proceeds from a resale normally go to the selling holder.

column2: Two institutions negotiate a price privately through a dealer network. What kind of venue is this?
column7: An OTC market connects dealers and customers through trading relationships. Electronic communication can be used in either OTC or exchange trading.

column2: A dealer quotes 49.70 bid and 49.90 offer. Before fees, what would 100 units cost to buy immediately?
column7: A customer buys at the dealer's offer. Multiplying 49.90 by 100 gives 4,990, whereas 4,970 is what the dealer bids for the same quantity.

column2: An order book shows substantial buying and selling interest at several prices around the latest trade. Which feature is illustrated?
column7: Depth concerns the availability of orders across price levels. Price momentum describes the direction of recent price moves.

column2: Which international body sets common prudential standards for banks across jurisdictions?
column7: The Basel Committee develops standards for bank regulation and supervision. Member authorities implement standards through their local frameworks.

column2: A country faces a near-term shortage of foreign currency for international payments. Which institution provides balance-of-payments lending?
column7: The IMF helps members with external payment difficulties. The World Bank focuses on longer-term development programmes and projects.

column2: Which project best fits the World Bank's long-term development role?
column6: Setting a country's overnight policy rate
column7: World Bank support includes long-term investment to improve living conditions. Short-term external payment support is associated with the IMF.

column2: How do central bank bond purchases normally transmit quantitative easing to the economy?
column3: Raise bond prices and lower longer-term rates
column4: Raise bond prices and raise longer-term rates
column5: Lower bond prices and raise longer-term rates
column6: Lower bond prices and lower longer-term rates
column7: Purchases increase demand for bonds, putting upward pressure on their prices and downward pressure on yields. Cheaper finance can encourage spending.

column2: Which action is expansionary fiscal policy when other policies remain unchanged?
column7: Extra government spending adds directly to aggregate demand. A policy rate cut works through monetary policy.

column2: Why can a central bank statement move long-term borrowing rates despite leaving today's policy rate unchanged?
column3: It can shift expectations of future rates
column4: It automatically resets existing fixed coupons
column5: It converts long-term debt into overnight loans
column6: It fixes the maturity dates of future borrowing
column7: Longer-term rates reflect expectations about the path of policy as well as current conditions. New guidance can change that path in investors' forecasts.

column2: Which weakness behind the global financial crisis did stronger bank capital requirements address?
column3: Too little capacity to absorb losses
column4: Too little disclosure of quoted prices
column7: The Basel Committee identified low-quality and insufficient capital as amplifiers of the crisis. Stronger capital provides a cushion against losses.

column2: A supervisor examines how several banks selling assets together could deepen a downturn. What perspective is being applied?
column7: Macroprudential supervision examines risks arising across the system. Actions that protect one bank can amplify stress if many institutions take them simultaneously.

column2: A securities exchange replaces its trading floor with electronic order matching. What still makes it an exchange?
column4: Prices quoted separately to each customer
column5: Terms agreed bilaterally for each trade
column6: A network of independent dealer quotes
column7: An exchange can operate entirely electronically. Its central trading arrangements and distribution of quotes distinguish it from a dealer network.

column2: Which authority supervises the safety and soundness of deposit-taking institutions in Hong Kong?
column7: The HKMA authorises and supervises banking and deposit-taking business. A bank's other regulated activities can involve other authorities.

column2: Which Hong Kong institution may accept public deposits of any size and maturity and operate current accounts?
column7: Licensed banks can offer the full range of deposit services, including cheques and current accounts. Other authorised institution categories face deposit-taking restrictions.

column2: An institution mainly conducts merchant banking and accepts large deposits of any maturity. Which Hong Kong banking tier is designed for this?
column7: Restricted licence banks principally conduct merchant banking and capital market business. Deposit-taking companies face an original maturity requirement as well as a minimum deposit size.

column2: What does the HKMA assess when taking a risk-based approach to bank supervision?
column4: Suitability of a listed company's sponsor
column5: Eligibility of a fund for public offering
column6: Compliance of an issuer with Listing Rules
column7: The HKMA examines risk management, internal controls and financial soundness to identify threats to stability.

column2: Which Hong Kong authority licenses corporations conducting securities dealing for customers outside the banking sector?
column7: The SFC licenses and supervises intermediaries carrying on regulated securities activities. Bank registration arrangements are distinct.

column2: Which body acts as frontline regulator for a Hong Kong listed company's compliance with the Listing Rules?
column7: SEHK carries out frontline listing regulation. The SFC oversees how the exchange performs its listing functions.

column2: A public offer of units in a Hong Kong retail fund requires product authorisation. Which regulator considers it?
column7: The SFC authorises relevant investment products and offering documents for distribution to the public. Registering a company does not confer that approval.

column2: Who oversees whether approved trustees administer Hong Kong's registered compulsory retirement schemes prudently?
column7: The MPFA regulates approved trustees and their administration of registered MPF schemes. The fact that a scheme invests in securities does not change that function.

column2: Which regulator grants Hong Kong insurance intermediary licences under the Insurance Ordinance?
column7: The IA is the licensing authority for insurance intermediaries. The HKMA exercises delegated inspection and investigation powers in relation to authorised institutions' insurance business.

column2: Which body registers Hong Kong audit firms to act as auditors of public interest entities?
column7: The AFRC registers local public interest entity auditors. The exchange's oversight of issuers does not include this registration.

column2: Who advises the Financial Secretary when he exercises statutory control over Hong Kong's Exchange Fund?
column4: Listing Committee of the Stock Exchange
column7: The Financial Secretary consults EFAC on control of the Exchange Fund and chairs that committee ex officio.

column2: Under the Basic Law, what is the Exchange Fund's primary purpose?
column3: Regulating the Hong Kong dollar's exchange value
column7: Article 113 specifies the Fund's primary currency role. The Exchange Fund is distinct from the government's ordinary spending budget.

column2: A foreign investor converts Hong Kong dollars and repatriates investment proceeds. Which Basic Law principle supports this?
column7: Article 112 protects free currency convertibility and the flow of capital into and out of Hong Kong.

column2: Who issues newly printed HK$10 notes for circulation in Hong Kong?
column7: The Government issues the current HK$10 notes. The three note-issuing banks issue other denominations, while older bank-issued HK$10 notes remain legal tender.

column2: What provides the reserve backing for Hong Kong's monetary base under its currency board?
column6: Shares in Hong Kong listed companies
column7: Changes in the monetary base are matched by changes in US dollar assets held in the Exchange Fund at a fixed rate.

column2: Banks call on the HKMA's strong-side undertaking. What does the HKMA deliver to those banks?
column3: Hong Kong dollars against US dollars
column4: US dollars against Hong Kong dollars
column7: At the strong side, demand for the Hong Kong dollar has driven it to the upper limit of its strength. The HKMA supplies local currency in exchange for US dollars.

column2: When the HKMA buys local currency at the weak-side undertaking, what happens to the Aggregate Balance?
column5: It stays at the previous level
column6: It changes only at month end
column7: Banks give Hong Kong dollars to the HKMA and receive US dollars. The contraction tends to put upward pressure on local interest rates.

column2: Why do Hong Kong and US interbank rates normally move broadly together under the linked rate?
column3: Capital flows respond to return differences
column4: The two markets share one interbank fixing
column5: Every Hong Kong loan is denominated in US dollars
column6: Local banks must match US retail deposit rates
column7: Cross-currency interest differences can attract funds. The adjustment mechanism links the two markets while still permitting a spread.

column2: After a US policy change, who decides a Hong Kong bank's best lending rate for customers?
column7: Local funding conditions influence banks, but setting a retail lending benchmark is a commercial decision for the bank.

column2: Which system links participating Hong Kong bank accounts and e-wallets for near-immediate retail transfers?
column7: FPS enables cross-bank and e-wallet payments at any time. The securities settlement systems serve different transactions.

column2: A merchant registers one phone number against several FPS accounts. Where does a transfer go if no account is selected?
column7: The recipient can nominate a default account for a registered proxy. The phone number identifies the recipient without requiring the payer to know an account number.

column2: A Hong Kong bank wants to test a new payments service with selected customers before full launch. What mechanism fits?
column7: The sandbox permits controlled trials with defined boundaries and safeguards. A trial does not confer blanket permission for wider rollout.

column2: A Hong Kong lender wants to use a firm's platform sales data to assess credit. What does HKMA guidance require before collection?
column6: Consent only once credit is refused
column7: The HKMA calls for informed prior consent and a clear explanation of how alternative data will be used. Governance still applies when a third party supplies it.

column2: An office manages investments, succession and philanthropy exclusively for one household. Which structure fits?
column7: A single family office serves one family's affairs. A multi-family office supplies services to several families.

column2: Which activity distinguishes a discretionary portfolio manager from a broker simply executing client orders?
column4: Obtaining a price for a specified order
column7: A discretionary manager decides how to invest within the agreed mandate. An execution broker handles the transactions specified by its client.

column2: A Hong Kong company appoints a sponsor for its listing application. Which regulated activity covers sponsor work?
column7: Sponsors fall within Type 6 corporate finance advisory activity and must also satisfy the sponsor-specific requirements.

column2: A Mainland visitor pays for a room in a Hong Kong hotel. How is this spending recorded in Hong Kong's external accounts?
column7: Visitors from outside the economy buy a service from a Hong Kong supplier. Purchases by Hong Kong residents visiting other economies are travel imports.

column2: An overseas exporter receives renminbi in Hong Kong for a sale to a Mainland buyer. What may it do with the proceeds?
column3: Keep them in a local renminbi account
column4: Remit them solely to a Mainland branch
column5: Convert them first into Hong Kong dollars
column6: Transfer them to the Exchange Fund
column7: Hong Kong's offshore renminbi market supports trade settlement. The exporter may retain, invest or convert the proceeds through a Hong Kong bank.
